competitive_implication: There is a large gap between the 24/7 promise and the actual after-hours customer experience. The shops making the promise are losing the exact calls the promise was meant to capture.
joke_candidates: The emergency apparently ends when the office closes.
Website at 2:13 AM: please fill out our contact form and we will get back to you. Bro really said emergency-ish.
The 24/7 emergency line goes to voicemail, which is technically a form of answering.
Open 24/7, except for the part where anyone responds.
The after-hours experience across nineteen websites is a phone number. That is the whole experience.
Nine shops promise round-the-clock help. Zero offer a way to talk to anyone after hours.
mechanism: Shops advertise emergency availability as a trust signal, but the website was built as a brochure: phone number, contact form, no after-hours path. Nobody built the 2 AM journey.
observation: 9 of 19 mapped Western Colorado shops claim 24/7 or emergency service. 0 of 19 show any live chat or real booking widget for the after-hours customer.
opportunity: Missed-call text-back plus after-hours intake (arbitrage Q1). A fast text response bridges the missed call and the human callback.

risk_notes: Medium because it implies broken promises. Kept fair by stating only observed facts and clowning the mechanism (the brochure website), never a business.
